sources.title: ONS Environmental accounts topic
facts: Current ONS environmental accounts hub; UK Environmental Accounts 2026 is the featured release.
Environmental accounts describe economy-environment relationships and include emissions, energy and natural-capital products.
Topic-level publication discovery is not a parcel emissions measurement.

sources.title: UK Environmental Accounts 2026 release
facts: Released 5 June 2026.
Release links 2026 emissions, energy-use and bridging-table datasets covering data through 2024.
A release catalogue is provenance and publication evidence, not parcel attribution.

sources.title: UK Environmental Accounts latest bulletin
facts: Latest bulletin is UK Environmental Accounts 2026.
Reports 2024 UK GHG emissions on a residence basis and industry/household energy-use context.
Residence-basis national and industry statistics do not establish territorial cadastral parcel emissions.

sources.title: UK Environmental Accounts 2026 bulletin
facts: Published 5 June 2026.
Reports 478 MtCO2e residence-based UK GHG emissions in 2024 and industry shares.
National/industry totals and shares are aggregates, not parcel observations.

sources.title: ONS greenhouse gases by industry and gas dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026 with data for 1990 to 2024.
Covers CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3 and total GHG by SIC industry.
Industry-level residence-basis emissions are not cadastral measurements.

sources.title: ONS greenhouse gases by industry current edition
facts: Current edition released 5 June 2026.
Page records scheduled revisions and a 2 March 2026 correction to earlier values.
Current/superseded edition boundaries must be preserved and not silently merged.

sources.title: ONS greenhouse gases by industry provisional edition
facts: Provisional edition is separately published from the current full-sector edition.
ONS states provisional estimates may later be revised as more data or methods become available.
Provisional rows must not overwrite final/current rows without edition evidence.

sources.title: ONS GHG emissions intensity by industry dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026 with current and provisional editions.
Dataset is an intensity product by economic sector rather than an absolute parcel inventory.
Intensity requires a denominator and cannot be treated as an absolute emission quantity.

sources.title: ONS GHG emissions intensity current edition
facts: Current edition includes a correction history and scheduled 5 June 2026 revision.
Correction and scheduled revision are distinct provenance events.
Intensity by industry is not direct parcel measurement.

sources.title: ONS energy use total dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026, covering 1990 to 2024.
Contains direct and reallocated energy use by industry from fossil and non-fossil sources.
Energy consumption is activity data and is not GHG mass without a compatible factor and scope.

sources.title: ONS energy use total current edition
facts: Current edition released 5 June 2026.
Edition history distinguishes scheduled revisions from corrections.
Industry energy use cannot be promoted to parcel GHG without compatible activity-factor and geometry evidence.

sources.title: ONS energy use by industry source and fuel dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026 with 1990 to 2024 data.
Breaks energy use down by SIC industry, source category and fuel type.
Source/fuel activity granularity remains aggregate and is not a parcel emission observation.

sources.title: ONS energy use by industry source and fuel current edition
facts: Current edition released 5 June 2026.
Provides downloadable current-version files and prior-version history.
Energy-use rows require separate emissions factors and valid time/scope alignment for estimated GHG.

sources.title: ONS fossil fuels by fuel type and industry dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026 with fuel use by SIC industry and fuel type through 2024.
This table excludes biofuels and waste from the named fossil-fuel breakdown.
Fuel use is activity data, not direct observed GHG mass.

sources.title: ONS fossil fuels by fuel type current edition
facts: Current edition released 5 June 2026 and records a March 2026 correction in prior data.
Current and superseded files must remain versioned.
Fuel quantity cannot become parcel emissions without compatible conversion and parcel binding.

sources.title: ONS reallocated energy use and energy intensity dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026, covering reallocated energy use and energy intensity by industry through 2024.
Intensity is usage per unit of economic output.
Reallocated/intensity statistics are not direct site or parcel measurements.

sources.title: ONS renewable and waste energy use dataset
facts: Released 5 June 2026 with 1990 to 2024 renewable and waste energy-use data.
Covers sources such as hydro, wind, solar and waste by industry section.
Renewable/waste energy activity is not equivalent to zero GHG or parcel GHG measurement.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric emissions bridging tables
facts: Released 5 June 2026.
Bridges UK Environmental Accounts measures with UNFCCC and UNECE measures for 1990 to 2024.
A reconciliation/bridge does not create new physical emissions observations.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric emissions bridging current edition
facts: Current edition records scheduled revisions to the bridging dataset.
Residence/territorial accounting boundaries must remain explicit across bridge calculations.
Bridging rows do not establish cadastral parcel attribution.

sources.title: ONS energy use bridging table
facts: Released 5 June 2026.
Relates UK Environmental Accounts energy measures to DUKES for 1990 to 2024.
A statistical bridge is a reconciliation device, not a direct meter or parcel observation.

sources.title: ONS energy use bridging current edition
facts: Current edition shows scheduled revision history through 5 June 2026.
Different energy-accounting frameworks must not be mixed without boundary alignment.
Bridged aggregate energy data remain non-parcel activity evidence.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric emissions road transport current edition
facts: Released 5 June 2026 with road-transport emissions data through 2024.
Page records revision/correction history for prior road-transport estimates.
National road-transport emissions are not land-parcel observations.

sources.title: Climate Change Agreements statutory guidance
facts: Updated 24 February 2026 with current guidance for the new scheme.
New scheme runs from 1 January 2026 through administration to 31 March 2033.
Eligibility, target and certification rules are regulatory evidence, not physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: CCA statutory guidance 2026 accessible webpage
facts: Defines target periods 7, 8 and 9 beginning in 2026.
Targets are set from base-year data and sector commitments with rules for new entrants.
Targets and baselines must not be interpreted as observed current emissions.

sources.title: Climate Change Agreements guidance collection
facts: Collection updated in 2026 and links current statutory guidance, technical annex and agreement templates.
Collection metadata helps establish current authoritative scheme documents.
Document presence does not quantify facility or parcel emissions.

sources.title: Managing a Climate Change Agreement
facts: Describes reporting of performance against CCA targets and 2026-to-2030 target periods.
Buy-out fees and penalties are compliance mechanisms.
Performance submissions, fees and certification are not automatically direct GHG measurements.

sources.title: Climate Change Agreements technical annex
facts: Updated 24 February 2026 for the new CCA scheme.
Sets technical rules for base years, targets, performance, buy-out and surplus.
Calculated scheme performance must remain distinct from directly observed atmospheric emissions.

sources.title: CCA umbrella and underlying agreement templates
facts: Updated 28 April 2026 and supersedes previous templates.
Underlying agreements apply scheme targets and obligations to participating facilities.
Agreement or facility identity alone does not create parcel-level emissions evidence.

sources.title: CCA biennial progress report for 2023 and 2024
facts: Reports progress of the CCA scheme and its energy-efficiency/carbon-reduction framework.
Scheme reporting includes targets, certification and reduced Climate Change Levy context.
Programme-level progress must not be promoted to parcel emissions.

sources.title: CCA 2026 extension to new sectors and processes
facts: Published 20 April 2026.
Extends eligible processes and updates the gas carbon-emissions factor used for buy-out calculations.
A scheme carbon factor and buy-out calculation are not observed facility or parcel emissions.

sources.title: CCA sector contact list
facts: Updated 17 April 2026.
Lists sector associations participating in the CCA scheme.
Sector participation/contact data are not emissions measurements.

sources.title: Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme guidance
facts: Updated 16 February 2026.
Explains ESOS qualification, assessment, compliance and published notification data.
Published notification data are records of notifications and are not necessarily regulator-verified emissions measurements.

sources.title: Comply with ESOS phase 3
facts: Current guidance includes action-plan and progress-update requirements through 5 December 2026.
Progress updates can report estimated energy savings for implemented measures.
Estimated savings and action-plan commitments must not be promoted to observed GHG reductions.

sources.title: Sustainability Reporting Guidance 2026-27
facts: Published 16 July 2026 by HM Treasury.
Sets minimum sustainability-reporting requirements for central government annual reports and accounts for 2026-27.
Reporting requirements and disclosed scopes are governance/accounting evidence, not cadastral parcel measurements.

sources.title: Greening government ICT annual report 2024 to 2025
facts: Published 16 July 2026.
Reports progress by government departments, agencies and public bodies on sustainable digital services and technologies.
Departmental or ICT footprint reporting is organisational aggregate evidence, not parcel binding.

sources.title: State of the Estate 2024-25
facts: Published in 2026 and reports central-government estate performance.
Reports aggregate GHG reductions and approximately 1.75 million tCO2e overall emissions for 2024-25.
Estate-wide totals cannot be assigned to individual cadastral parcels without verified allocation and geometry evidence.
